candidates.rationale: Normaliser swap. B divides the daily range by $open, a price level, so its second leg is just a relative-volatility sort that re-ranks structurally volatile names; A gives location but no intensity. Replacing the normaliser with A's 21-day ceiling turns the range into the fraction of the remaining gap to the monthly high that today's bar covered, bounded in (0,1] and large only when range expansion actually carried price to the top of the 21-day range. The accrual rank then loads that breakout-completion measure on earnings quality: attention-grabbing pushes to the ceiling in low-quality names. Keeps TS_MAX($high, 21) from A and ($high - $low) from B, 3 nodes each, so no 4-node overlap with either. Also drops A's mix of adjusted $close with raw OHLC; this is raw-scale throughout.

Standardisation. Both parents carry a risk level: B's ($high - $low)/$open is today's volatility print, A's TS_STD($return, 126) is the six-month volatility level, and the two rank the same high-vol names. Dividing one by the other cancels that shared level and leaves what neither parent has, a range surprise: today's range relative to the name's own volatility regime. The accrual rank supplies the quality tilt, so the factor is a quality-conditioned volatility shock rather than a volatility sort. Inherits TS_STD($return, 126) from A and ($high - $low) from B; the multiplication is structured as rank x (ratio) rather than (rank x range)/... so it shares no 4-node subtree with the pair-1 child either. Units are clean: a raw-OHLC ratio over a return-based vol, no adjusted price mixed in.

Path normaliser: an efficiency ratio. A normalises displacement by the range envelope, so a smooth advance and a chop that ends in the same place score identically; B compares true range to summed range over two days only, so it has a path notion but no horizon and no location. The child takes A's 21-day floor as the anchor, B's short-window extreme as the tip, and B's summed-range structure lengthened to 21 days as the denominator, giving net displacement per unit of path travelled. That is a trend-quality measure neither parent can express: A is location-only, B is two-day overlap-only. Shares TS_MIN($low, 21) with A and TS_MAX($high, 2) and ($high - $low) with B, 3 nodes each; the 21-day TS_SUM does not match B's 2-day one. Raw OHLC only, so A's adjusted/raw scale mix is gone.

candidates.changed_node: root: product of centred RANK($roa) with A's ceiling drawdown, over B's range width
candidates.rationale: Interaction instead of a difference. B subtracts a location rank from a quality rank, so quality and location never interact: a high-ROA name at its high scores the same as a junk name in its trough. A has the location machinery but no fundamental. The child multiplies centred quality by drawdown from A's 21-day ceiling, so quality is only paid where the name has actually pulled back, and junk that has pulled back is shorted rather than ignored. B's TS_MEAN($high, 21) and TS_MIN($low, 21) supply a robust range width, which also fixes B's weak normaliser (its price-level denominator is nearly constant per name, so its location leg is dominated by price scale). CS_DEMEAN(RANK(.)) centres without spending a free constant. Inheritance is 3 nodes to each parent, no 4-node overlap with any archive member.

Sign plus horizon. B (9d3a08) is a ratio of positive ranges, so a two-day gap up and a two-day gap down look identical to it; B (ef9533) has no horizon past today's bar. The child measures the two-day upward extension, TS_MAX($high, 2) - $low, against the week's path length, which makes it an extension measure rather than another volatility print, and times it by the accrual rank so the extension is only traded where earnings quality argues the move should give back. That is a timing conditioner neither parent has: accruals are a slow signal with no entry rule, the overlap ratio is a one-to-two-day microstructure statistic with no direction. Inherits TS_MAX($high, 2) from 9d3a08 and ($high - $low) from ef9533, 3 nodes each; the 5-day TS_SUM avoids matching the 2-day one in the parent and the 21-day one in the pair-3 child.

candidates.changed_node: numerator: (TS_MAX($high, 2) - $high) as a signed reversal term, gated by centred RANK($roa)
candidates.rationale: Direction from the fundamental. TS_MAX($high, 2) - $high is the one-day shortfall from the two-day high, a short-horizon reversal that 9d3a08 can only see unsigned because its ratio is built from positive ranges. Centred ROA rank supplies the sign and 1a7135's TS_MEAN($high, 21) with 9d3a08's TS_MIN($low, 2) supply the width that makes the shortfall unit-free. The claim neither parent can make: short-term reversal is worth taking in high-quality names and is a trap in junk, which 1a7135 cannot say because it adds quality and location rather than multiplying them. Fragments are TS_MAX($high, 2) and TS_MIN($low, 2) from 9d3a08 and TS_MEAN($high, 21) from 1a7135, 3 nodes each; the 2-day floor in the width keeps the denominator distinct from the pair-4 child's.

candidates.changed_node: denominator: (TS_MEAN($high, 21) - $low + 1e-8) replaces A's price-level normaliser; root becomes a product
candidates.rationale: Bad cross, stated rather than forced. Parent B is a strict sub-expression of parent A, so it contributes no variable A does not already carry, and it is a two-node tree, so no child can share the three nodes the crossover check demands from every parent; this pair cannot pass mechanically whatever is proposed. What is still worth keeping is the substantive weakness in A: its location leg is divided by TS_MEAN($high, 21), a price level that barely varies within a name, so the leg is mostly a price-scale sort. The child divides by a range width instead and turns A's difference of ranks into a product, so quality gates the reversal rather than sitting beside it: junk gets near-zero exposure, quality gets full exposure to trading below its monthly typical high. Treat this as a mutation of A, not a fusion.

candidates.changed_node: root: centred RANK($roa) crossed with centred CS_RANK of B, sign flipped
candidates.rationale: Fusion is nameable but the pair still cannot pass. The interaction is limits to arbitrage: the quality premium concentrates where liquidity and attention are thinnest, so centred ROA rank times centred liquidity rank is a real term neither parent has, and the negative sign says quality pays most in the least-traded S&P names. Double centring makes it a pure interaction, near-orthogonal to both main effects, which is what a cross into a different niche should add. The mechanical problem: parent A is RANK($roa), a two-node tree, so the largest subtree any child can share with it is two nodes, below the three the crossover gate requires. Parent B is inherited whole, TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21), 3 nodes. Note also that B's level alone is close to a size sort, so it is used only as the conditioning axis, never as the signal.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

In the rationale, state the fusion logic: what does the combination capture that
neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.

  B [ef95334c229839b8]  CS_RANK($accrual_gap) * CS_RANK(($high - $low) / ($open + 1e-8))

  B [ef95334c229839b8]  CS_RANK($accrual_gap) * CS_RANK(($high - $low) / ($open + 1e-8))

  A [97dfe9ddfd2178f6]  ($close - TS_MIN($low, 21)) / (TS_MAX($high, 21) - TS_MIN($low, 21) + 1e-8)
  B [9d3a08c718d8b572]  CS_RANK((TS_MAX($high, 2) - TS_MIN($low, 2)) / (TS_SUM($high - $low, 2) + 1e-8))

  B [1a7135b2fcfcb338]  RANK($roa) - RANK(($open - TS_MIN($low, 21)) / (TS_MEAN($high, 21) + 1e-8))

  A [1a7135b2fcfcb338]  RANK($roa) - RANK(($open - TS_MIN($low, 21)) / (TS_MEAN($high, 21) + 1e-8))
  B [8f22297f2ea21a91]  RANK($roa)

pair 8
  A [8f22297f2ea21a91]  RANK($roa)
